text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) After initial euphoria, I have to say that the ROI is marginal at best. Briefly, here is why:

Positive:
1. Excellent day and night picture quality
2. Simple configuration and UI.
3. Free storage up to limit.
4. Rugged construction
5. Integration with Smarthings and other IoT.
6. Easy setup. Ensure you buy the condoms and mounting brackets for outside.

Negative: (Relative to price point)
1. Battery life is marginal. If you never have motion in an area great. But, think about that front yard where you have people walking by or cars parked just on the edge of your property. With roughly 10-15 activation per day, the battery drains quickly. I feel I would be better off with a perm. powered device.
2. While it has a standard micro usb port similar to virtually any android smart phone. You still require the Arlo plug to charge. Not a deal breaker, but painful.
2. App load times/camera viewing is slow. I have a 100 mb Xfinity internet connection with Netgear Orbi Mesh setup within 15 ft of the front camera. Connection in my house is not the issue. I have a Samsung S7 device. Be prepared to wait upwards of 30 seconds before authentication, app loads AND THEN the camera activates to see who is at the front door. It needs to be faster.
3. The absolute worst aspect of the camera is that recording does not start fast enough. Roughly 30 seconds of an event (or more) go by before capture begins. This is not acceptable. I have tried playing with various settings but unable to resolve.

Overall, I regret purchasing now. I should have invested the time and installed a fixed camera setup.

12-Jul-17 - I have lowered the stars on this product because of the incredibly poor support provided for both this product and in particular the ORBI which I also have. The warranty on both products which are similarly priced make zero sense. Stay away from NETGEAR until they get their act together.

17-Aug-17 - Finally heard back from NETGEAR and received confirmation in their user forums that the original screw adapter on the VMA1000 mount for the solar panel is too big. (gee thanks..I knew that) I was sent new screws that now allow the solar cable to be plugged in along with the VMA1000 mount. Why these are not highlighted everywhere and why there is no update to the Amazon listing as a bulletin or something to look for when buying the solar panel, I don't know. Overall, I would say NETGEAR is completely lost on any form of cohesive support and sincerely hope my product continues to work as I do not want to ever have to call or email again..

June 2020
I am done with Arlo. The product is over-priced and unreliable. Here is why:
I added the doorbells 2 yes ago and 2 of 2 have been rma'd.
2 of the cameras have been rma'd.
1 of the 2 solar panels has apparently died as not properly charging. This after less than 2 years.
I only realized recently that some Einstein at Arlo decided to have the wifi channel operate on the exact channel my mesh is on. There are clearly issues.
The camera has good and bad days from an access perspective. Some days they come up in about 30 seconds. Some they don't load..
The delay of 5 seconds before motion activates recording is brutal. You can completely someone moving fast.
Arlo support has become poor after being fantastic initially.

This product will be going the way of my Orbi soon. I am done with Netgear ( or formerly Netgear) products...
text_fidelity_b: Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130)

text_fidelity_a:
Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black Some appear to have had some difficulty or confusion with assembly, but I did it solo fairly quickly with no issues and found the instructions very clear. No tools were needed and all of the pieces went on smoothly. The direction sheet clearly shows and lists what pieces to use. I guess some didn’t see that one of the shelf sections is thicker. The stand appears quite sturdy and stable. Yes, the only real issue is if you’re using the discs at the feet. I guess the bare, spike type feet ends are supposed to be for thick carpet. Like many I had mine on wood/laminate flooring and so need the small discs as the spike tips will surely scratch it up. This isn’t really a problem per se, but it is quite finicky and it the only part of the operation my wife had to assist with. It definitely would’ve been nice if they’d just included both a spike and attached foot type tips with the stand especially at this price. I included two pics with this review that I took while in the process of getting it and components situated. The stand easily fits my vintage Sansui 661 receiver on the middle shelf and Audio Technica LP120 turntable on the top. I hope both this review and photos showing it with the perspective of having components on it help.

Edit: So, yea, I did dock a star due to the feet issue. As I noted they are finicky, but can quickly get frustrating. While I had to move the stand around getting my stereo stuff sorted the small discs constantly came off and you just really can’t put them back in solo. They will and did put small indentations on my floor with the discs off. My solution was to pick up a 4 pack of 1” sliders from WM that are plastic on the bottom with an adhesive disc on the top. I then stuck the small metal discs from the stand on the slider. Once my wife helped me place the discs back on the legs it could then slide pretty freely and they stayed on. It’s a shame they didn’t include a normal leg along with the pins. I still like the stand quite a bit, but I’d warn people with mobility issues against this one even as nice as it is.
text_fidelity_b: Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Spot - Smart Alarm Clock with Alexa - White The major reason for buying the SPOT over the echo 2 is that it can act as a tabletop alarm clock. I LOVE the idea of this however gave it 2 stars because Amazon has not executed the program design well. If you are not right on top of the SPOT, you cannot even see the time on the clock. Amazon, are you listening? I bought this assuming that you will correct the issues with the SPOT that have been clearly articulated by many people before me on this site. You are good at what you do, so I am still hoping. I will list the major issues again assuming that someone from your design team will reconsider

1) There should be a clock face option that is LARGE and fills the Spot Screen so it can be seen across the room and in the dark.
2) There should be an option to turn off the flashing of the temperature and other information.

That's it! From my perspective, not too much of stretch to make the SPOT go from 2 star to an 5 star.

Also, I noticed that someone replied defensively to another reviewer challenging them on his or her low star review. The challenger asked how you could rate an item so low that did so many other things so well. It made me chuckle as it almost seemed like something an entrenched Amazon systems designer would write. This is what I would say to them: The only reason I bought this little tabletop item as opposed to the echo 2 with better sound is to have Alexa and a clock together in one device on my nightstand. Time to go back to the drawing board and fix this one folks.

July 7, 2019
I went to manually turn off an alarm on the Dot and now it is flickering continuously. I have read all the troubleshooting items and performed them to no avail. In my opinion it is a hardware issue. All I did was pick it up to manually turn off the alarm. Shoddy engineering to go bad like that. So disappointed Amazon. YOu are so amazing in so many ways, but people don't want to buy something that is going to go bad after 14 months even though gently handled. My friend also has an echo show that started flipping the screen with duplicate images. No fix for that either. There is a pattern here Amazon. Please take note.

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130) Arlo is not perfect, but it is wicked close.

What's Great: You can put it anywhere within range of the link/router. The alerts are reliable, if a little slow on the uptake. The picture is good. Set up was simple and worked the first time. A reasonable amount of cloud storage is free, and it's easy to download whatever you want to save. The cameras are easy to move around to wherever you need them, and you don't have to set them up again.

What's Okay: A person who walks fast can get through a room almost faster than Arlo can start recording. Now, it's still much faster than an old Belkin Netcam HD, which sends pictures of where the motion WAS. Before the picture. And the D-Link 930L, which is a fine monitor cam, but has never been able to send a snap or a clip, no matter how many times it has been set up to do that. However, both of those cameras have audio and stream reasonably good images via their apps (the Belkin video resolution is way better than the Dlink). That makes them okay monitors next to smart security sensors - if the sensor alerts, you can look to see what tripped it and listen to see what's going on. Arlo will - most of the time - catch whatever set it off and let you know within seconds. And it's free, not an extra $$$ feature.

What Could Be Better: The link thing is enormous. It could be a little less expensive. And it would be WONDERFUL if it integrated with Z-Wave or Smart Things. The plan here is to station the Arlo cams near other devices that send push notifications - Nest Alarms, Smanos smart sensors, etc.

How It Compares: Beats the Canary I couldn't get to activate. Way better than the other netcams in the house. Love it. Just added another camera.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130)

Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch Immediately, I realized I love these headphones. I'm not in love with the color, and I'm perplexed why companies always say something is for iPad, etc., although I suspect it is just the "cool" thing to do. I have no apple devices, but this worked immediately and perfectly for my Blackberry 9700, Xoom, and Win7 Laptop.

The first device pairs by itself, and devices 2-8 pair by holding 2 buttons for 5 seconds. After that, if multiple devices are turned on when you turn the headphones on, it seems to want to pick the first one you paired it with.

The BB picks it up as a Logitech Wireless Headset (not something generic), and you can then control the volume with the BB or with the headset itself (Did I mention the controls are all well positioned on the right headphone? - just two volume buttons, mic mute, micro USB charging port, and LED indicator), and you can also toggle between BB speaker phone and headset - they are obviously fully compatible - not generically. Pressing the mute button give you an audible cue, but does not change the BB display.

You'll never catch me in public with a normal bluetooth earpiece on anyway, so this is also great for calls at home - it will cancel out more background noise (because of the foam on both ears) so you can comfortably concentrate on your call. My tests show it working well more than the claimed 10m away (of course that partly depends on the other device's radio as well).

As another reviewer said, these sound good (and are capable of getting louder than I'll ever need), but are probably not as great as the full over-the-ear headsets. BUT, the wireless capability is really great to keep you fully uninhibited when exercising, cooking, or whatever you're doing when talking on the phone or listening to your music. For the record, I am 100% opposed to wireless shelf/tower speakers in a real home system, but this is a great solution for a headset.

Also, the mic backing out of the way is a must, so thankfully that is included. It not only pivots, but flexes toward or away from the mouth as well - very good design. Finally, the folding feature is great; any space saved is important. And the connecting wire connecting the two sides is accessible, if all that bending ever has it in need of a replacement.

Past helmet use has me thinking my skull is about as large as they come, and these are comfortable on me with the sides fully extended.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch

ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This is a very easy to use timer with some features that I’ve not come across before. It offers three main modes:

1) Clock – standard digital clock
2) Count up timer – can count up from zero to time events. It counts in whole seconds, so it’s not a true stopwatch.
3) Count down timer - you can set it to count down to zero.

The three modes are set by a sliding switch on the left so it’s very easy to change between the modes. It also has a memory feature so you can store a value and re-use it. For example, I use the count down feature to time tea brews, and have set a value of 3 min into memory. To repeat the countdown all I have to do is press the memory button and it sets itself to 3 min.

The best feature is that you can turn off the beep! There are three notification methods: a standard beep, vibrate or a flashing red LED. That’s a huge plus since I usually carry the timer with me and find the beep to be very annoying. The light or vibrate options are far nicer to use. I would imagine the flashing LED light option would be especially appreciated by the hearing impaired. You set the notification type with a switch on the back.

The overall build quality feels very solid. The numbers are large (about 0.75 inches tall) and easy to read even though the screen is not backlit. There a clip on the back that includes a magnet, so you can position this on a fridge or stove hood. The clip does not detach, but the profile is low enough that it doesn’t cause a problem if you want to carry the timer in your pocket.

It runs on 1 AAA battery (included). The package is easy to open – no clamshell to have to wrestle with.

It’s a well-made timer with some great convenience features built in. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer Logitech makes the best universal remote controls and they keep introducing new models that are better and better. If you have half a dozen (or more) remote controls on your living room table and are always losing some of them or forgetting which does what, then a universal remote is for you.

The Harmony 950 appears to be mostly the same as the Harmony Elite, except without the Harmony Hub device. The Harmony Hub can be purchased separately later, though the Elite package is cheaper if you're getting it anyway. The Harmony Hub greatly expands the range and capabilities of your Harmony remote, so you should think twice before skipping it.

Logitech also sells much cheaper Harmony remotes without the touch screen. The main benefit of the touch screen is to program shortcuts to your favorite TV channels and to control more devices than the non-touch remote controls can access. If you always use your DVR or cable box's on-screen channel menu and only have a few devices, then maybe a much cheaper Harmony without the touch screen is a better value for you.

The Harmony is pretty easy to program by connecting to your PC and connecting to the Logitech website. If you have an older Harmony remote, you may be able to transfer all your device settings to this one. The buttons on the Harmony are easy to see, well spaced and give you good feedback when pressed.

Battery life is OK for a touchscreen device, but like your smartphone you will need to recharge this at least every couple of days. Most people will leave the Harmony in the recharging station most of the time, so make sure you have an electrical outlet close to where you will be using the Harmony.

If you're in the market for a universal remote, Logitech Harmony should be first on your list. The only decision you have to make is which model to buy. If you're trying to control a handful of devices (TV, cable box, DVR, stereo system, game system, DVD player), then you really have to ask yourself if the touchscreen feature is worth the big price premium. If you have a "smart home" with remote controlled lights, outlets, thermostat, etc or if your devices are spread around a large room so the IR remote has trouble connecting with them, then the Harmony Hub is a good idea.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk 8GB Clip Sport MP3 Player, Blue - LCD Screen and FM Radio - SDMX24-008G-G46B UPDATE: 11/15/14 Just found out that you can NOT transfer overdrive (library) WMA format books. I didn't realize it earlier because all the books I'd put on it were in MP3 format which do work fine, but some library books only come in WMA and apparently the sport only supports DRM free WMA, which means not library books.
UPDATE: 11/8/14 Wound up w/problems w/this clip & had to return for replacement. Was w/in 30 so did thru Amazon & just got new one in. Will see how it works. This happens occasionally w/clip+ & zip so not too worried. Still think the clip+ is the best, followed by the zip, then the sport.
UPDATE: 10/5/14 I have since found the Pause delay has gotten much worse than when I 1st tried it & can last way too long like others said - sometimes about 15 seconds when resuming play - which may not sound like much, but it is. It becomes very problematic in that it takes so long you don't know if you pushed play again or not. If you push it again too soon then when it finally does come on it immediately goes off again. Sometimes it's taken me up to 6 tries to get it right & that is ANNOYING! Also, it tends to go to have a delay before playing after you FFWD, which again can cause the same problem. And, as others said, the FFWD is Very Slow. Sometimes when I try to FFWD I have a pause issue & then somehow it goes back to the start of the book & then I have to start all over w/the FFWD - again - very irritating. The bigger screen seems a waste too, as the book cover is shown in a tiny square that's hard to see. In the zip it fills the whole screen & is actually bigger, so what was the point of the larger screen? I don't know who at SanDisk could actually think all these usage & design changes were good ideas, as far as I can see they've only come closer to ruining a good thing. If they wanted a new & improved clip, they should've kept all the features & workings of the clip+ & just added a larger color screen, a more durable clip (& a longer battery time is always nice), but changed nothing else. Each newer model, even the zip, but especially the sport has taken away more than it's gained. For the meantime, I've reduced it from 4 to 3 stars & must say the sport model is the worst of the 3. I'll be writing to Sansa support to see if there is some sort of software fix. If there is, I'll revise this review again.
------------------
Original Review:
Works fine with audiobooks. Read a number of bad reviews & 1 that said couldn't use with library's Overdrive Media system, but I did not have any real trouble with it. Yes, it's true, doesn't have a MSC setting, but I xfr'd books from OM w/no problems. The only difference was I normally make a new folder under audiobooks & name it w/book title, series # & author's name. When I made a new folder it wouldn't let me name it. Instead I simply chose Audiobooks, then in the first box where that showed, went in and typed a / then how I wanted sub folder to be named, then continued as usual. It make the sub folder as I named it and xfr'd the files there. When I checked my books folder, they were all there under the folders I'd named that way. I'd had this same problem once before with a clip zip, and it's not a major impediment, it's actually a bit faster, really.

With Audible, I've never been able to activate or deactivate a device, I always have to contact them to reset. Also at 1st it showed the internal drive space as the external drive space even tho no card was in the clip. I chat'd them & they logged onto my pc, activated it, renamed the drive it was showing as & now it works fine. They even fixed another problem I'd had w/Audible software crashing when I tried to delete books on any of my clips. They said the drive identification problem was specific to the clip sport, but they fixed in in almost no time & I would've had to call them regardless of which clip type I bought. It is slightly bigger, about 1/4" taller, 1/8" wider & 1/16" deeper but it's still darn small & the bigger screen makes it a bit easier to read. I haven't tried in sunlight but I can't read either the clip+ or zip in sunlight either, I just find or make some shade. I listen only to audiobooks so I can't comment on playlists or other music functions.

Re the power button, I don't have a problem w/it working, but I would prefer a separate button, don't know why it was removed. Re the pause/play delay. Yes, there is one. It's about 1-3 seconds from pressing pause & about 2-7 seconds for pressing play again. I didn't find it to be an extremely long delay, but again, would prefer they fix that issue but it's not a deal breaker for me, I just have to remember to wait those few seconds & not try pressing the button again too soon! I can see where if you are doing something where you're operating the functions w/o looking it would be irritating.

I haven't tried copying cd books that I've ripped w/windows media player, but I know that the order always gets messed up with clip zips, so I've always only used storage on micro cards with the clip+ for those books. They changed something when they made the zip & I'm guessing the sport won't be different, but I'll add a post if I find differently. I use the zip & now the sport for Overdrive & Audible. I always keep 3 clips at any given time as they tend to die in about a year of daily use (2-10/hrs per day) and any Overdrive books I've stored for them can't be put on a different clip, but they're cheap enough that works for me. The clip mechanism breaks sometimes (I have 2 working zips now w/broken clips) but I then use 2 part epoxy & glue a potato chip clip on and they don't last as long but can always glue a new 1 on as long as the clip works. Also, sometimes a clip dies & if holding down the power button for a long time doesn't work, I've found if I wait a few days sometimes then I can connect to usb on pc & it starts working again.

Yes, all clips have specific issues and the old clip+ is still my favorite and I'll always keep 1 of them that works, but for the other 2 I get what ever's on sale at the best price. I wanted an 8gb this time because I don't like to put Overdrive books on storage cards & it was only $10 more than a 4gb clip+ (for some reason their price has gone up recently). I, too, hope Sansa keeps making the clip+ because it's still the best one out there (because it can play copied cd books) but to me the zip & sport are pretty equal except for the mildly annoying pause delay, but if I can get an 8gb sport for same price as a 4gb zip, I'll live w/that! Sansa CLIPS are still by far the BEST & CHEAPEST & ONLY SMALL MP3 players that work well for audiobooks, so I'm still a loyal customer. ALSO THEIR CUSTOMER SERVICE IS VERY HELPFUL. They always replace any that break w/1 yr warranty, they help w/problems even after & sometimes can fix by updating software, etc. So for all those folks who had a problem, call Sansa before you give them a bad review! I use them for many hours every day & have for years now, so I know of what I speak. (Also, don't ask me why, but I've found the purple clip+ tends to have tighter audio jacks which cause static if headphone is not fully connected & it's harder to push jack all the way in, so just stay away from the purples - tho they will replace it if you have problems. Never had any trouble like that with black, blue or red one's.)

Yes, the developers have cheese for brains & the only 'improvement' in the newer models is larger screen w/color & graphics which can make book identification by cover image easier to figure out even if can't read type & the other changes in my opinion make them not work as well as the clip+. Those differences may not matter with music, but do for audiobooks. Each type has some flaws (& battery time is never as good as advertised, I'd say 8 hrs for clip+ & zip) but they're still better than anyone else for a no hassle, easy to use, tiny clip that you can wear w/o dragging on clothes or falling out of pockets & their prices can't be beat! I've looked & looked over the years & have never found anything better. So I still say thanks to Sansa for making the clips!
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk 8GB Clip Sport MP3 Player, Blue - LCD Screen and FM Radio - SDMX24-008G-G46B

Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310 You should know up front that this extender only works wirelessly with dual-band WiFi routers (routers with both 2.4GHz and 5GHz).

But it will work as a hard-wired range extender for single-band routers (2.4GHz) using an ethernet cable.

If you have a single band router like we do, it will not detect the wireless network or connect wirelessly. If our neighborhood is any indication, this extender won't work with most home routers. Out of the ten or so visible wireless networks in our area, the extender only detected one or two. The two it detected were two of the weaker signals, but I assume were dual band signals the extender would work with.

After several frustrating attempts to get it connected wirelessly, I spent about an hour with customer support before being informed of this limitation on the extender. The product listing says "compatible with all Wi-Fi routers," and it may be compatible with all routers if set up as a wired extender, but apparently it isn't compatible with all as a wirelessly connected extender. If you want wireless connection to your router, check your router's capability and make sure it is a dual-band router before ordering.

As I mentioned, I did get it set up as a wire-connected extender using an ethernet cable. And it works well for that. It puts a good strong WiFi signal all over our house and much of the yard. I'm giving it four stars for that.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310

Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW), I own ALL of the kensington line of trackballs (clearly a trackball nut). From the original Expert Mouse (using a serial connection) all the way to this one. I can see how some purists are very touchy about their trackball performing and as it becomes an extension of interfacing with the computer, it's critical that it performs well.

PROS:
* Nice compact footprint; Not too demanding for space.
* Comes with the little ergonomic squishy thingy for a wrist-rest.
* The ball 'stays in' the unit even if you turn it over! This is a new concept for their trackballs! (you can pop it out if you need to condense for travel)
* Scroll wheel is nice; A feature present only in the higher-end trackballs.

CONS:
* BUTTONS! YUK! The button has some kind of contact issue where if you press it gently enough, you hear and feel a little 'click' but you didn't actuate the button! You must press it harder, and get a louder firmer CLICK! (really kinda mushy) to click it! I have tried different spots on the button and it's all the same! This is ALMOST a deal killer for me, but I'm going to give it some time, see if the button wears in and that false-click goes away over time.
* Scroll wheel is not free-flowing like on the modern expert mouse. With that sucker, you can fling the wheel and it will roll atleast for a half-second or so! This one really resists movement so it's more like a mouse-wheel than a scroll-wheel. It does not have a 'ribbed' feel, it rolls smoothly but it's not a 'on rails' as other models.

My personal favorite is still the modern expert mouse. It's massive (like a little tank on your desktop!) but you can navigate quickly with it, and use it in the manner a trackball was designed to be used.

Hope my review helps you!
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW),

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K1000 Manual Focus SLR Film Camera with Pentax 50mm Lens My k1000 will be 30 years old this Christmas, and it has been the most reliable camera I have ever owned. My lenses are still nice and sharp. My light meter and flash shoe still work. I have probably changed the battery 3 times. There are no light leaks. Everything works just like the day I got it.

This is a great first camera for any person who wants to learn about photography: exposure, composition, etc. With digital point and shoots, it's really easy to just be a documentarian and rely on photoshop or filters to fix things up a bit later, but there's no real incentive to get things right in the first instance. Film - real film - requires patience and discipline and a critical eye. Which is why I am teaching my 11 year old son to use this.

A tip on loading the film (I was dead broke for a lot of the first decade I owned this and could not afford to waste a bit): Before you try to load the film, bend just the last little bit down, so that it makes a little l-shaped piece that will catch in the slot. Put the tag into the slot and carefully pull out just enough to fit the film snugly into the camera. BY HAND, turn the spool on the left side about half a turn to set the film on the spool and make sure the holes are caught on the teeth. When you turn the left spool, the film should come easily out of the canister. Only do a little bit, and if it seems to be working (i.e. pulling the film out of the canister), close the back of the camera. Cock the camera - WATCH the film counter to make sure the film is advancing. If it's not, don't rewind unless you are sure you can do so without losing your leading edge into the film canister. Just open the back and re-set the edge onto the spool and try again. If it is - and you should be able to feel the resistance in the mechanism - shoot a picture. The first one won't come out. ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This timer is a good size with a very readable LED display and a strong magnet on the clip on the back to hold it to your fridge or whatever a magnet will stick to. The buttons are large and accessible, and it's really no problem to set it up. It beeps loudly when the time is up, so there's little danger you're not going to hear it from an adjoining room.

Strangely, on day one (unlike with some timers I've used), the first three or four times that I held down the hour, minute, or second buttons to speed up the counting and turn off the beeps, it just froze and stopped counting. If I pressed the button over and over to advance the counter by one, it worked—beeping annoyingly loudly each time, of course. I was about to give it a two-star review and throw it away because I couldn't stand it, but I put off doing it and just stuck it to the top of my stove. A week later, after I'd used the stove several times and the timer probably got exposed to some heat, I went back to try it again so I could write this review and the fast-count sans beeps feature worked. Weird. Maybe it was just stressed in shipping and needed time to settle down....

A few things I really do dislike is that it's easy to reset the time by mistake if the grey button on the left gets slid up; the modes are manually set with this button. (That approach to the modes could be good for the technologically challenged, though.) Also, if you overshoot your mark on the time, there is no way to go backward; you have to go forward until you come back around to where you were supposed to have stopped the first time. The clip is a little too sharply angled, so when you stick the timer to a surface with the magnet, the face slants down somewhat, but it's still visible; really not that big of a deal.

Another thing, as I've remarked about another MeasuPro product: the how-to info on the packaging is white letters on light grey, which is practically unreadable for anyone, not just people like me with old eyes. (The company told me they were correcting that with the other product, so I expect they will do the same with this one.)
text_fidelity_b: ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger

I had this product suggested to me by a friend who was using it for two screens with our work laptop and it seemed to be working fine. I only used it for one screen in the beginning and the very first thing I noticed with it was that it would become very warm or hot to the touch after less than an hour. I used it for a few months and the next thing it did was cause my mouse and screens to lag behind during operation. I then purchased a camera that I tried to plug into this docking station and everything went even more haywire with the camera, mouse and screens both acting up when operating my laptop, and of course the device was always warm to hot. So, I stopped using it and just direct wired everything to my laptop, which is extremely inconvenient when I need to move my laptop around, and I don't have enough ports to plug things in. Then, my husband bought a new CPU and needed to plug his two screens in so I let him try this docking station, and it wouldn't even register with the CPU at all. I plugged it back into my laptop where I knew it did work at one time, and sure enough, it doesn't work anymore.

So, basically it didn't function the way it should have, and within 6 months it just stopped working all together. Biggest waste of money, and now I can't return it.

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

I had to use a separate diplexer to join my UHF and VHF antennas since this didn't provide both inputs. Unlike my other amp, though, this has an LTE filter built in - a product of its newness. The power injector is much simpler and smaller than my other one had been, with the actual transformer in the plug itself. The short length of cable is much thinner than RG6, however, which makes me wonder if that is a source of db loss. Anyway, seems to work just as well as my other one. Even though I watch very little TV containing commercials, I quickly noticed how annoying it was to not have instant background noise.

Signal gauge is just a bit gimmicky, at least in my case where I'm pointing between two cities and trying to get as much as I can from each, which doesn't equal maximum signal according to this gauge. But that's okay. Use "TV Fool" and a compass, and you won't need a gauge, but it won't hurt.

text_fidelity_a:
PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37 Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

One thing I sadly use a lot of – phone/USB cables for charging and data transfer. These are almost as bad as the AUX cables for my car and iPod.

So, seeing this was a Philips one – I honestly thought I lucked out. I was going to give my old cable to my mom as hers was cracking near the "C" port. I figured I could use this one - she could have my old one.

It is a DURABLE cable and looked like it would go through quite a bit. The length is perfect for charging with an adapter connected to a power strip on the floor. And, it can also plug into the USB ports on a computer (or so equipped power strip).

So, why a one star rating?

This does not work. I tried with my phone and my mom’s phone. NADA. Nothing. I tried connecting it to the adapter – nothing. Tried using just the USB cable to a USB port on a power strip (which was on since it is powering my computer) – NOTHING.

So, I tried using a USB port on my computer. NOTHING. Tried with a “USB hub” connected to my computer. There was a slight problem. The “buttons” on the port light up when a port is turned on. Despite the port for this cord being on – the lights didn’t light up. Other items connected – my external mouse and a USB flash drive – they were turned off when this cord was connected.

Needless to say – this is BELOW one star. It doesn’t even work. But, I do have to rate it something.

I could’ve gotten a bad cable – after all, there is no damage to it or the packaging. But, it still doesn't work. But, I can’t return it since it was free.
text_fidelity_b: PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37

I could hear clearly with the caller and there was absolutely no outside sounds interfering and the caller could hear me clearly as well. The case is so compact and stored easily in my bag. The pieces are extremely comfortable. I sleep in mine so that I can listen and no one will be bothered by it. This is the first pair that are this small to actually stay in my ears overnight. text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones, Anbes Wireless Earbuds, IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earphones with Ear Hooks & Mic, HD Stereo in-Ear Headphones Gym Running Workout, 8 Hours Battery Noise Canceling Headsets When I first got these, I had a problem with the left earpiece not having sound, and the sound that came from the right ear was very tinny. Customer service was absolutely wonderful to resolve this for me very quickly. Since then, the sound is great! I have really small ears and I do find them a bit too big, even with the smallest cover, which keeps me from wearing them as long as I'd like. I haven't actually tried them in wet conditions, so I can't speak to this, but they are very well made and seem like they will last a long time.
--Pros
*Even though I was worried about the earpieces not being switchable, because I am left eared, this has worked alright when I am driving. I just hang the left earpiece on my shirt and use it with my right hand to work the controls.
*Charging is very fast.
*A charge last quite a long time, especially if you only use them for calls. Even listening to music it last a long time.
*The sound is nice and loud with lots of bass for listening to music.
*Call sound quality is great, for me, and for the listening party.
*The are easy to keep up with, using the nice case that they came with. It slips right into my purse or other bag.
*Well made. Durable and made with quality materials.
---Cons
*The earpieces are too large for my ears, even with the smallest cover, and my ears start to hurt after a short time.
*The pieces that go around your ears is shaped in a way that the bottom pushes into the back of my ear, causing it to get very sore.
*They are a bit larger and heavier than I'd like them to be.
*It would be nice to have a small clip for when you are driving, so that you can clip it to your shirt, to be hands free.

Overall, these are great headphones. They need a little tweaking, especially on the earpieces to make them more comfortable on the ears, but I would still highly recommend them.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones, Anbes Wireless Earbuds, IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earphones with Ear Hooks & Mic, HD Stereo in-Ear Headphones Gym Running Workout, 8 Hours Battery Noise Canceling Headsets

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Illuminated Ultrathin Keyboard K740 with Laser-Etched Backlit Keyboard and Soft-Touch Palm Rest - Black This is a very attractive and comfortable keyboard. The keys are fairly responsive (I'd rate them a 7/10 on responsiveness) and have a feel halfway between laptop and regular keyboard. Their noise is diminished when compared to most gaming keyboards but there is still a distinctive soft sound (it's actually quieter than the sound your fingers make if you just lightly drum/tap them on a keyboard without actually typing. Except for the space bar and enter key which are a little louder).

Aesthetics-wise, it is very attractive, the clear plastic edge gives it a nice finished look (though it's of course functionless and breakable, it would protect the keyboard itself and is a seperate molded and attached piece. The lighting is customizable to four settings - off (num lock and caps lock remain on at full brightness at any setting), and then backlights on- low, mid, and high. In general I prefer low lighting and have sensitive eyes and get migraines, and the low setting is pleasant, the higher settings are fine unless you're in the pitch dark and then It's too bright for me. In bright light the top setting is still nice and visible.

The keyboard has all the functions and options like print screen and page up and down and mute/volume controls that I need. I haven't used all of them yet.

The palm/wrist rest is not padded but is comfortable and does have a "soft" feeling coating. It does has sturdy fold out upper feet.

The cord is approximately 71 inches (180 cm).

This is a very slim and comfortable low-profile keyboard that is full size and has great back-lighting options. If it came in multicolor backlighting for a similar price I would've purchased that one as well.

I bought this for a new Lenovo Y910 AIO Win 10 which hasn't arrived yet (thanks UPS for making me wait 3 MORE days now when I paid for 2 day prime shipping), but I tested it on my MSI GE70 laptop running WIn 7 Pro and it was literally plug and play, worked instantly.

The bottom row of keys (ctrl, windows, alt, spacebar, fn, ctrl, are much taller/raised which is a little weird at first (arrow keys and number pad keys match the rest of the low profile keyboard). I may just be noticing it because I have damaged extensor tendons in my dominant left hand which limits how high I can lift 3 of my fingers. Time will tell if I get used to it and stop noticing it.

I've uploaded many photos, one is a composite showing all lighting settings. The differences are much more apparent in person than I could capture on camera.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Illuminated Ultrathin Keyboard K740 with Laser-Etched Backlit Keyboard and Soft-Touch Palm Rest - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310 My experience with this extender has been good; it's significantly strengthened the signal in our living room, at the other end of the (admittedly not very big) house from our router. The one thing I've noticed is that nearby electrical devices, and especially ones with motors in them, will definitely throw this extender for a loop. We have an air purifier that lived first next to this extender, and then at a point about five feet from the extender, but between the extender and the router, and the extender did not like either of those situations at all. Lots of orange-light action (an orange light on this extender means no wifi signal). Moved the air purifier well away from the extender and out of the signal path and all was hunky-dory again.

I'm geeky sometimes and would like to be able to log onto the extender and muck with settings or at least make sure everything's good beyond what the green light tells me, but I don't seem to be able to do that once the extender's been set up; I can only get to the setup/configuration page after resetting the extender using the button on the back. But I'll live. The extender seems to be doing what we expect of it, and that's...all we expect of it (funny how that works).
text_fidelity_b: Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310

text_fidelity_a:
Cooler Master MasterBox Q300L Micro-ATX Tower & Thermaltake Toughpower GX2 80+ Gold 600W SLI/Crossfire Ready Continuous Power ATX 12V V2.4/EPS V2.92 Non Modular Power Supply Only two issues are that the stock fan that comes with the case is not quiet, and there is no area for a disk drive. Everything else about this case is pretty cool. Cable management was much easier than the other three cases I have worked with. HDD/SDD management is really neat--it's behind the motherboard instead of at the front base of the case, saving precious room for large GPUs if that is your thing. His computer is not RGB, but this thing would look darn cool with RGB.

I really like how the case is the size of a mATX case, but it can comfortably fit a standard ATX motherboard due to the ability to change where the PSU goes.

At this moment, I cannot speak for how cool the case keeps yet, but the whole thing is essentially a grate, so I can't imagine the air flow being bad. I suggested he get a few more fans just to keep air flowing through the filters, as they impede flow a fair amount, just like all the non-foam filters I've dealt with. If need be, the filters can be easily removed to allow the system to cool more effectively.

If I need to get a new case for some reason, I will probably get this.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation This is a great streaming box! Like the title says, it's a ROKU on steroids. I have an Apple Airport Extreme router and the ROKU would "occasionally" start buffering because of the processor; however, with the Amazon Fire TV, that's not an issue because it has a quad-core processor. Great streaming box!

Updated 5-4-14 I've had the Fire TV for a couple of months now and for the most part it's great; however, today we rented "Bad Grandpa" on Amazon. It played great but when there was 35 mins left in the movie, it quit playing. Tried to restart the movie and got a message saying there was a problem with playing the movie and to contact Amazon Customer Service. I called them and they said that when this happens, "...unplug the Fire TV for 15 seconds and then plug it back in." In my opinion, that takes the fun out of watching a movie! I thought the memory and quad-core processor would be enough to stop this from happening, wrong! Having said that, instead of naming my review "ROKU on Steroids" I should have named it "Just like ROKU".

The Amazon rep said that it was a problem with the memory of the Amazon Fire TV and not the video. When asked if the problem could be fixed by Amazon with an update, all he said was "I'll forward that to Amazon".

If you don't mind watching videos that stop playing and having to unplug the Fire TV and restart it during a movie, you'll really like the Fire TV.

One other point, the Amazon rep stated that it might be my router. I have an Apple Airport Extreme, the best and fastest available. If it was my router, I guess the Amazon rep should have had me unplug my router instead of the Fire TV. He finally admitted that it was the Fire TV and not the router.

Just wanted to get this information out there so people can be informed about the Amazon Fire TV before purchasing one. All in all, I'm happy with the Fire TV...just aggravated that I have to unplug it and restart it when watching movies. The Amazon Fire TV should be better than this!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show 8 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone I purchased this for two reasons: a convenient way to display recipes that didn't require my phone being out, and streaming movies for when I'm in the kitchen for hours at a time.

I rely heavily on streaming during the holiday seasons while I bake to fulfill orders, and while the video quality was good, and the sound was AMAZING, the rest of the device was too troublesome to be worth it.
Example: Open amazon video, and it gives you 4 categories to go through, or your library. I go to my library (severe lag every single time) and I find the movie I want. I hit play, severe lag again, and it plays. Quality is not bad at all, especially for the price, but heaven forbid you have to pause. Once you pause for ~2-3 minutes, it goes to a screen saver. And when you unlock it, you have to go through the process of finding the movie all over again. It's a pain in the butt. They could at least have a "continue watching..." at the beginning of the prime menu, but it doesn't.

Secondly, our household has 3 users on our hulu account--if there was a way to switch users through the Echo, I didn't see it. I googled it, thinking I was overlooking it, and nothing. We all have very different tastes for shows/movies, and never use each others accounts for this reason. To have not one, but two streaming services being out of the question/too inconvenient to use, I couldn't handle it.

The integration was wonky at best. I have an echo dot that resides on a window sill about 3 feet from where I had my echo. My echo was off for voice recognition, but when I'd talk to my dot, it would display on my echo. This was cool except for two things: 1. It did it intermittently. 1 out of 3 times it would mirror to the echo. 2. if you were streaming something when the echo mirrored what the dot was telling you, guess what, YOU HAVE TO FIND THE MOVIE AGAIN. It was a nightmare.

Maybe down the road they'll figure out a more user friendly programming for this, but until then I'm returning it. It was meant to be a gift for family, but if I, an electronic savvy 30-something, can't figure it out, I wouldn't be comfortable giving it to my grandparents, which was the end goal.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show 8 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone

For those of us w/ a LOT of media, Plex is the pinnacle of enjoying your own media with the best interface possible (and it's free); whereas KODI is the best way for streaming media from the internet. The Shield recognized my old archives instantly, and also when I plugged in a USB3 SanDisk flash drive for extra space. I've had 3 WDTVs, 2 Nexus Players, and 1 MiBox, and I wasted all of that time and money until I got this. I've KODI Phoenix and Exodus for internet streaming, and Plex for my 200 movies, 25 seasons of TV shows, 75 instructional videos (on guitar, magic, and yoga), 6k songs, and all my family albums and artwork. I have the Plex client (player) for TV, phones/tablets, XBox 360, Chromebooks, and Chromebox.

The Shield has BOTH the Play Store and the NVidia Store on its dashboard. I can play all my games again because this console doesn't stutter and freeze up. I'd missed my Asphalt 8 when the others just couldn't handle the workload anymore. I can get even better games from the NVidia Store that the Play Sore doesn't have. Of course, all previous purchases come right back to the Shield --like the HomeRun HD. Plex has a deal they're making w/ HomeRun HD to possibly turn the shield into also doing DVR.

The gamepad has been totally redesigned and has gone from an Ugly Duckling to being prettier than a pail full of kittens. The hex-grip feels good in the hand for shooting zombies or driving on racetracks. The gamepad is rechargeable (yay!) and even comes w/ it's own charging cable. The once $50-extra remote is now included w/ the console. Like the gamepad, the remote also has a headphone jack for discreet listening and a touchscreen volume control and Mute.

Of course I have other Wi-Fi devices. That should NOT be a problem.

This is NOT ready for prime time … no pun intended.

I do NOT intend to have to set up this device every couple hours.

text_fidelity_a:
CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW) These are pretty much as basic an RCA cable you can find that will extend the length of your existing RCA cables without the need for another male-to-male adapter. While for components that have RCA hookups that allow you to use any RCA cable that your can find, I would recommend buying a single longer cable as every connection point is a place for potential signal loss. However, for components that have their RCA cables integrated with the device, you have little choice but to buy an extender such as this. Turntables, especially the older variety, are the most notable components that have this configuration, and since most people like to be able to play records from a location that is easy to reach and has plenty of headroom, this is often far away from your receiver and the built-in cables on the turntable are usually far too short for this. This is why these cables are a perfect way to add an extra 3' while only introducing one additional connection in your linkage, where using a standard RCA cable with a male-to-male adapter introduces two.

Also, since the cables which are connected to turntables are almost always of bare-bones quality with the minimum gauge of copper necessary to carry a signal (that's assuming the wire is made from copper at all, and not from some other cheaper alloy), these are probably going to be the same gauge. Your connection is only as good as the weakest link, so buying some thick gauge cable that is made out of magnetically polarized copper probably would only serve to drive the price up with no actual benefit to you except for being able to brag about them. Therefore, this RCA cable extenders is all that you really need and will spare you the embarrassment of spending money on something that you actually do not need at all. Some "high end" users might complain about them being of a small gauge because they have convinced themselves that they have to use overpriced Monster cables to connect their gear to be able to fully enjoy it., but I don't necessarily buy into this. True, good cable makes a difference, especially when you are sending a signal over a longer distance (10' or more) chances are the mid-grade cable of 16 gauge copper wire with gold plated contacts is all you're going to need. This cable solves your short cable problem while telling the world "I am care about how my music sounds, but I am neither a sucker nor a fool!"
text_fidelity_b: CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW)

Echo Auto (1st gen) - Hands-free Alexa in your car with your phone I have a 2006 Volvo S60R (with a factory sound system and 10cd changer and cd player but no aux no usb, etc) and I have a Samsung Note 10+ (I've had Notes since the Note 3 and am one of the millions angry about the loss of the built in AUX). I've had my car 2.5 years and initially installed a GROM aux adapter ($70)-Volvo 01-07 Auxiliary Input Adapter Kit) because at the time I had no faith in bluetooth so I declined the even more pricey $140-"Select Volvo 01-07 Bluetooth Hands Free Car Adapter Kit". Now with my newest phone I'm hating that I have to chose between audio or charging. I've been watching the price of the bluetooth grom adapter, but then amazon notified me that this Echo Auto was discounted to $19 and I wondered if it would work instead.

My top priorities are sound quality and ease of use. My car has an exceptional sound quality as is. I watched some review videos and though no one could confirm if it would do what I need and do what I need hooked into the existing grom adapter. For $19 it was worth a try.

It comes in a little box with everything you need. I ignored the vent holder and the aux cord and took it and my phone out to my car. I took the aux from my grom out of the aux to usb-C adapter that goes into my phone and plugged it into the Echo Auto. I took the power cable and attached it into my existing usb power supply. It powered on quickly and lights started flashing. I added the device in my phone's alexa app. It went through the set up (wants location and bluetooth access at all times). It then played a test sound and then considered itself a successful install even though the test sound only played out of my phone's speaker not the system. It even told me I could unplug and get rid of the aux cable as it wasn't needed. I then spent a drive struggling to get it to work. The aux cable IN MY CASE is definitely needed for it to work. Eventually when I had force closed the alexa app several times and fought with it to just open something to play (it wants you to only use alexa type stuff- music on amazon music or audible books). It wasn't until I ran my errand and came back into my car and turned it on that it automatically loaded and started to work.

To be clear, I want to listen to my music (on my phone's samsung app), or listen to youtube videos (on my phone's youtube app), or listen to podcasts (on my phone's beyondpod app), occasionally I will also use the audible app.

I don't want to talk to it or use it as I would my echo dots in my house. The only linkable music services available in the alexa app are a)apple music, b)spotify, c)pandora, d)deezer, e)siriusxm, f) tidal, and g) vevo.

95% of my music is on my samsung music app but if you plan ahead and get stuff in external apps going before you are ready to drive you can do it.

One thing that annoyed me is that when I did use a recognized source (audible), it stayed in my status bar and you can't get rid of it you just have a pause and play button, you have to swipe and close multiple alexa app windows to get it to go away.

The music quality is perfect (but this is likely related to my grom and has nothing to do with the echo auto). I am super thankful I found a cheap option that lets me play audio via bluetooth to my car stereo from my phone. I realize I'm not using it for what it's meant to be used for (voice command and alexa use) but I did do some testing and with windows at least half down and my car's eVolve exhaust system it worked about 85-90% of the time.

It never asked me about my amazon/alexa/echo/google accounts at all so you have to set your home and work from scratch.

In conclusion, this would likely be less complicated for someone who's system is less complicated and it seems to work as it's supposed to and is malleable enough to trick it into working in circumstances it wasn't meant to.

First edit- after a few days' use- it's impressive how I can leave my car and then return and start my car and it just starts playing. I listened to my podcast in my house using a random bluetooth speaker, turned off the speaker (podcast player auto stops), then got all my stuff and went out to get in my car (already on, warming up) and it started playing the podcast again through my phone when I was still 6 ft away. I can't get my phone to restart playing where it was on any of my echo dots or bluetooth devices/computer in my house, heck a phone call or notification stops playing half the time and it manually needs restarting.

Update 7/2021

My only complaint is that if I disconnect Bluetooth on my phone it WILL NOT reconnect again unless I unplug/turn off the echo auto and then it auto reconnects. Just turning Bluetooth back on on my phone means it will never connect back without this extra step
text_fidelity_b: Echo Auto (1st gen) - Hands-free Alexa in your car with your phone

I don't particularly care about the complaints regarding gigabit limitations etc. When I get fibre with equivalent speeds to my house or need to stream ultra HD some day, then I'll worry about it. In interim, HD video streaming, surfing, gaming etc..all work flawlessly.

Comments for WD PowerLine owners:
1. WD utility is unable to pickup on speed of the TP-Links (Rate Mbps). This is an application issue obviously and not completely sure if I can get around this as of yet.
2. I have not secured or modified network name as of yet which made things easier. Hope this does work when I get to it.
3. Ensure you have space for the bulky plug in unit. Not really an issue if you take the bottom wall plug.

For everyone:
My WD PowerLines were collecting dust until I moved. My previous home had a different circuit setup that prevented any PowerLine units from working correctly. They would see each other, but speeds were like dialup. So, don't be ticked if these do not work.

My new house has limited drops and roughly 3k Sq Ft over 2 floors and have no issues. My WD's have over 160 Mbps indicated on the utility from top to bottom.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AV200 Nano Powerline Adapter Starter Kit, up to 200Mbps (TL-PA2010KIT)

text_fidelity_a:
NexFoto 32GB Large 15 inch Digital Picture Frame, Wi-Fi Digital Photo Frame, Wall-Mountable, Instantly Share Photos Videos via App or Email, Gift for Father's Day This digital frame is a really nice size for displaying your photos. It can store a lot of them, and it has a decent brightness so you can easily see them even in a brightly lit room. The plastic frame isn't the nicest looking in my opinion; it would be nice if they offered different color and style frame options. I will probably end up painting my frame- I haven't quite figured how I plan to do that yet, but I just want it to look less like modern black plastic.

The app is really, truly terrible. It's difficult to figure out, it will only upload a few files at a time, and it takes forever, so if you have a lot of files to load, take my advice and don't even bother with the app. Just put them on a micro-SD card and load them that way.

Navigating the onboard menu is difficult, and I didn't find the directions to be very helpful. I was eventually able to get it figured out, more or less. There are some things that just don't make sense; for instance, in the main menu you can set the slide show to display the time each photo is shown. However, this doesn't actually do anything as far as I can tell, because after setting it the images will still flash by at 15 second intervals (this seems to be the default) until you go into the menu for the individual folder you are showing from and set the time intervals there. And the time options there are different than they are on the main menu; for instance, the main menu allows you to set 1 minute intervals. The folder menu allows 30 seconds and 2 minutes, but not 1 minute. So I'm not sure what all that's about.

Once you get it set up right, the picture looks very nice. It has an optional sleep mode you can set, and it has a motion sensor function you can enable if you like, but what I really wish it had was an ambient brightness sensor so that it would dim itself when the room is dark, and brighten itself when it gets brighter. This would be such a huge upgrade, especially for bedrooms, or TV rooms, or anywhere else where you want it to be dimmer when it's dark and brighter when it's bright.
text_fidelity_b: NexFoto 32GB Large 15 inch Digital Picture Frame, Wi-Fi Digital Photo Frame, Wall-Mountable, Instantly Share Photos Videos via App or Email, Gift for Father's Day

text_fidelity_a:
Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Compact Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Set 2.4G Ultra-Thin Sleek Design for Windows, Computer, Desktop, PC, Notebook, Laptop (Black01) I think this set is very cute in terms of design with some hidden features that is not marketed. So here is what I think.

Build Quality & Design:
I think the color is personal preference, but still think the white-pastel baby pink theme is very cute. Other than that, it doesn't have any unnecessary design element. The finish material is somewhat cheap plastic, but when you consider for $15 keyboard AND mouse set, it is extremely well done. As you can see from photo, they prepared USB-B home on the back, next to battery. Most other companies do that under the mouse, so this was very interesting choice of design. Definitely, it is somewhat inconvenient, if you have to use this set in multiple computer. Other than that, it doesn't bother me at all.

Functionality:
Again, this is somewhat personal preference, this keyboard makes very low hitting sound except the spacebar. I have no idea why they built this way. So it is too much for silence keyboard because of the spacebar but it sounds very dull if you like to hear the mechanical sound of typing. This keyboard doesn't have 6 key island (insert/home/page/delet/end key, normally placed on top of cursor arrows.) If you need for these keys frequently, then this keyboard is not for you. It does have fn-key function so you can use these keys somehow, but it's somewhat inconvenient. Also, they placed backspace twice (one in the conventional place and in the number pad under + sign. This set needs 4 AAA battery, which I think it's a little excessive.

Ergonomics:
Both the keyboard and mouse are very thin, so it feels somewhat inconvenient. Especially the mouse looks and feels very similar to the old apple mouse, adding considerable pressure on wrist. If you are okay with Apple mouse then you will like it. (But not me.)

Buy it if you need : a set of keyboard & mouse with limited budget with extremely cute colors
Don't if you want: ergonomic, full keyboard or if need to use your computer for long time
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Compact Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Set 2.4G Ultra-Thin Sleek Design for Windows, Computer, Desktop, PC, Notebook, Laptop (Black01)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers I tried the first generation Kindle but didn't really care all that much for it. While I loved the screen, it just didn't feel right, and remember thinking this would be perfect if it had a touchscreen.

When the Touch was announced I ordered this along with a Fire with the thought that the Fire would be for me, and I'd give the Touch as a gift. The Touch got here this morning and I opened it up just to make sure it was OK. It looked so nice that I carefully peeled off the plastic just to try it out for a few minutes. After all, one wouldn't want to give a gift that didn't work, right? Well, it's now been a few hours and several chapters of a few books later. I'm keeping it. A second one will be on order for Christmas giving.

Why keep the Touch when I also have a Fire? If you skip over the obvious answer (I just love electronic gadgets) the e-ink on the Touch is much better in terms of clarity and lack of glare. Not that the Fire is bad. It has a very clear screen, but there is some glare. The Touch is better for reading under all lighting situations, and remains highly readable in direct sun. I can't imagine getting better screen clarity than this for black and white text.

I also tried reading it while on a treadmill (a situation that usually gives me a headache when I tried it using the kindle app on my Touchpad) and it was quite pleasant. Best of all is that I can zoom up the text size so I can read it while it is on the treadmill reading stand (it's too far away for me to read hard copy unless it's in HUGE type. Getting old is _not_ fun).

But the strength of the Touch is also it's biggest problem for me - black and white. I read several magazines each month and reading them in B/W is lackluster at best. Magazines are more enjoyable on the Fire, especially publications such as Wired.

The touch interface is great. So far its been very smooth and glitch free. Love the feel of the screen - has a bit of texture to it. I have to say, however, that I am a bit concerned about the screen longevity. The Touch overall feels a bit fragile and less "solid" than the Fire. I'm not deducting any stars for that since it's just an impression, but it will be interesting to see if the durability of the Touch screen is better/worse/same as the Fire (and vice versa). I'll be getting a case for it for sure since it's going to be getting bumped about.

I'll be using the Fire mainly at home and for reading material that works best in color (and, of course, video - need to relax the mind with mindless entertainment as well!). The Touch will be living in my briefcase for reading while commuting (I take the bus and subway, so lots of time to read) and for killing time prior to an appointment. The longer battery life and smaller size makes it a better traveling companion than the Fire. I don't have the Touch 3G version, so I'll have to make sure I keep a few books on my to-be-read stack so I don't run out when I'm out of wi-fi range.

Granted, if I could only have one device, I'd stay with the Fire since that offers more entertainment options, albeit at twice the price. But the cost is not excessive, so I treated myself to both. With a Fire and a Touch I've got all bases covered (until, of course, the next glittery gee-whiz piece of electronics comes out...).
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers
