RUBAN Notebook Lock and Security Cable (PC/Laptop) Two Keys 6.6 Foot (Black) This notebook lock and security cable works with laptops that have a Kensington security slot (about 99% of them on the market do), so it will work for most notebooks except the MacBook Pro. Be sure to check to make sure your laptop has the security port which looks like a small slot usually found in the upper right outside corner.

To use this cable run the end of the cable around a fixed object that can't be moved without effort or drawing attention, such as the leg of a heavy table or a post, then loop the locking end through the loop and attach it to your laptop. The locking mechanism has a built in bar that fits into the Kensington slot, so just insert it into the port, then turn the key 90 degrees to lock it in place. You'll need the key to unlock it when you're ready to take the laptop so be sure to bring it along. When you want to remove your laptop just rotate the key in the opposite direction to unlock it. This set comes with a spare key as well in case you misplace one.

The cable that comes with this is 6.2" long which wasn't long enough to go over the top of my desk and come back up to secure my laptop to the desk that way, but it was adequate to secure it around one of the desk's legs, so this cable isn't intended to permanently affix your laptop to a desk top, and it's thin enough to cut with bold cutters, but it's long enough and strong enough to deter someone from being able to snatch and run off with your laptop when you're at the library or coffee shop and want to leave it unattended long enough to go use the copy machine or go get a refill!

I like how the T-bar mechanism works to secure the lock to the laptop but still allow complete cable movement and rotation without dislodging the lock from the laptop, and I also like the fact that the cable is coated to prevent damage to your laptop & whatever the cable is secured around. This laptop lock and security cable is going to be perfect for my daughter when she studies in the campus library.

I received this notebook lock and security cable for testing and review. It works a lot easier than I expected!

Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest. I really wanted to love this keyboard. In fact, I have purchased three of them over the past 18 months. If it weren't for the fact that two of them simply stopped working altogether with the steady red LED problem along with complete lack of function, I would probably have given this deice a 5 star review, and that is all of the variants that exist of this keyboard. When it works, it is a wonderful device. The problem is, there are clearly some major quality issues.

First off, what is it about this keyboard that is so fantastic that makes it so popular if it has so many problems? Answer, it feels wonderful, and when it works, it's a dream. It is the right shape and size even for practically all typically sized hands. Maybe even for some of the more tiny-handed men out there. Microsoft has perfected the bezel curve of the ergonomic keyboard in the Sculpt, and the amount of travel it gives each key is perfect. The feedback of the keys (as in the feel) is perfect as well. The apparently physical quality of the device seems well made (if though it clearly has some design flaws). Even the amount of "clack" that the keyboard makes is satisfying without being obnoxious.

So what's the problem? Aside form the things people have talked about ad nauseam (broken keys, losing that tiny transceiver means the keyboard is useless, etc.. being the seemingly biggest issues) so along with practically all of Microsoft's consumer-grade products, support is nowhere to be found. While MS offers comprehensive support plans for their corporate products, you are on your own with accessories, even if they are expensive bluetooth accessories. They don't even host proper forums for their accessories (there is no category for this on their official forum) and any information elsewhere on the internet about the Sculpt is strangely scant, so trying to find out what the steady red LED means is definitely a no-go. Anything I find is either for another model or simply doesn't map to this condition. Therefore, I can't even find out what the red LED light even means, let alone attempt to resolve the problem. Their phone and chat support offers no meaningful help as they are unfamiliar with the device. Since I have a Mac they balk and say the device isn't supported on a Mac, even though I have been using it for 9 months beforehand without incident. Also, the red LED turns on immediately after the new batteries go in so it's probably nothing to do with signal and a failure of the device itself. This seems further evident since the bottom of the keyboard that is underneath the light actually gets warm to the touch, so I should assume the keyboard is fried. This would be the second Sculpt keyboard that this has happened to in less than a year so this is not an outlier. I don't do anything to my keyboards that would kill them like this. My old Logitech Wave that I keep having to go back to keeps on ticking.

Also, note that apparently USB 3 interferes with the wireless signal between the USB dongle and the keyboard, a problem I have personally experienced when my keyboard strangely stopped receiving input temporarily for a few seconds and then resume. I thought I solved the problem by using an old USB 2 hub to get the dongle physically closer to the keyboard as I thought it was a reception issue that is so common with Bluetooth devices. (I am not even sure if this even uses Bluetooth and it might just be some proprietary RF signal.) But in fact, I later learned that it was the use of a USB 2 port that was far away from my USB 3 ports!

Sadly, as tantalizing as this device may be, I would steer clear of it. It's nothing but trouble.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest.

The manufacturer claims that it supports multiple devices at the same time, that it has a long range of 490 feet, that the battery charge lasts "all day," which most of us would interpret as 8-12 hours or more, and that it has a noise-cancelling microphone and enhanced speakers to create "crystal-clear calls" in noisy work environments.

I have tried to pair it to both my phone and TV transmitter at the same time, and the TV transmitter does pair if the phone is paired. The range isn't as far as advertised. The battery charge lasts about 4-6 hours. It has excellent sound quality for receiving calls and listening to TV, but persons on the other end of a phone call often complain that they have trouble hearing me, so the mic doesn't work very well. This headset is really uncomfortable to wear, making it difficult to use it more than an hour. Also, be aware that the rechargeable battery is not replaceable when it dies.

I actually have a headset with similar functions that cost me about 1/5th the price, so I'm not convinced this product is worth the extra money.

I purchased the power charger and things seem to be better. However, when I plug it in to charge, it does not always start charging and I have to unplug it, wait, etc. And now I noticed that it isn't holding the charge very well. I called Amazon and they are sending me out a replacement right away. If the replacement doesn't have any issues, I will keep the 5 stars and assume i got one with a glitch. It happens. If there are still issues, then it will be an overall problem and my ratings will drop. There was a person on the forum page that also had this problem. Most others are reporting no issues with the battery. So for now, I will gave Amazon the benefit of the doubt.

I have only had this for a day so I have not explored everything. This is my first tablet so I have little to compare it to, but I have a Kindle e-reader which I love. I found this to be pretty user friendly considering I don't even have a smartphone so apps and touchscreens are new to me. I found the user's guide to me helpful as well as the Kindle forum to answer questions I didn't feel like looking for answers to. I had no problem uploading my favorite sites. Some said they couldn't watch movies but I have been able to with both Netflix and Amazon on demand.Also, I guess there were some issues with the sound in the first generation Fire. I didn't have any problems, I didn't even need to use full volume when watching shows.
I downloaded a few free apps to play around with. And of course my books. I like that I can download some to the Fire but if there is one I want to read that I already own, I can download it from kindle Cloud. I can read books without downloading them via the Cloud but that means keeping the wireless on. Same with music.
I'm not to great with touchscreens and I loathe fingerprints so I prefer to use the stylus that I got separately. I didn't get a charger (it comes with USB cord only but charging through the computer won't really work), the one for my Kindle fits but doesn't charge as fast. So I ended up ordering the fast charger as the Fire isn't meant to last as many hours as the Kindle e-reader. But I still think the battery life is pretty good.
I like reading on this, I thought the back-light would bother me, but I can adjust the brightness. I actually prefer reading in the portrait mode as it shows two pages and looks like a book page would.
So far I am very happy with this, my third Kindle device. I like Amazon and find them to be very user friendly when I need help so I have no concerns so far. If there are any issues, I will update my review because I take spending my money very seriously.

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57) I bought this because I was traveling abroad and I wanted to backup my phone pictures. If my phone got lost or stolen on the last day of the trip, I would lose all my pictures from the entire trip. It's definitely better to backup your pictures each evening so they most you could ever lose would be the pictures from 1 day. You would still have the rest.

This is mostly just an issue when traveling abroad. Back home where WiFi is common, the iCloud backup is just fine. Unless you take zillions of pictures, you can even use your cell data to backup your pictures when there's no WiFi (assuming you have a reasonable data plan). However, when traveling abroad or on a cruise, access to the cloud can be quite expensive and/or limited. That's where this device comes in handy. Backup your pictures without WiFi or cell data.

There is another reason why you might want this device. If you take tons of pictures on your phone, then space can be a problem. You might be running out of space on your phone and/or the cloud. Or maybe you don't have an iCloud account at all. You want to make room on your phone, but you also want to keep all the pictures. You can copy your pictures to this device, and delete them off the phone to make room for more pictures.

The concept of backup up pictures from your phone is a good one, but I don't think this device is the best way to do it. I just bought the RAVPower FileHub wireless travel router, SD card reader, USB portable drive companion. I think that's going to end up being a better solution than this device.

There are a couple of things I don't like about this device:
1) The drive is very wide. If you have two USB ports that are close to each other, the drive will block the other port.
2) I find the connection to the iPhone to be awkward. The lightning connector on the device is on the end of this flexible rubber arm on the side of the device. You bend this arm away from the device (but not too far, per the warning in the instructions), and plug it into the phone. It's hard to describe, but you end up with this thing at an awkward angle hanging off the bottom of the phone. You wouldn't want to put it in your pocket like that, and it sits funny on the table since both the phone and the device are at an angle. If you flip the device around, you can get the phone to lay flat on the table, but then the device is blocking the home button. It's a really goofy design.
3) This last one takes a while to explain. There is a sync mode, where you can automatically sync the device with your phone. This will save any new pictures from your phone onto the drive. Here's how it works: You run the app, plug the device into the lightning connector, and run the sync. Pictures are copied to a folder on the drive that you specify. Since you create the folder originally, and you associate the phone's sync with that folder, you can use the device with multiple phones. Simply use a different folder for each phone. When you sync, any new pictures on the phone which aren't already in the sync folder will be copied to the drive. The concept is very good.

However, one huge drawback of the sync is that the file named aren't preserved. For example, if you just copy a picture off your phone using some other method, you'll get something like "IMG_2841". That's an easy name to deal with, if you want to do something with a particular picture (e.g. Bob wants a copy of IMG_1531, or I want to print an 8x10 of IMG_2316).

Unfortunately, when you use the sync method, the file names are not preserved. The picture files get really long names with a seemingly random string of characters. I'm sure the names mean something to the sync program, but for a human they just look like random garbage. In any case, your drive ends up with this sync folder filled with hundreds (or thousands) of files with random unreadable names. If you want to do anything with the files, you'll wish they had more recognizable names.

Let's say for example that you copied IMG_1000 and IMG_1001 off your phone using some other method, and later you decide you also want IMG_1002. Well, you know that the picture must be in the sync folder, but good luck finding it. You wish you could just sort by name and grab IMG_1002 directly, but since the names are all random you'll need to scroll through hundreds (or thousands) of thumbnails and try to figure out which picture was originally called IMG_1002.

Because of this issue, I think the sync mode is useless.

However, you can still back up your pictures in a semi-manual way. The trick is that if you do a manual copy to get a picture from the phone onto the drive, then the original file name is preserved. So, instead of doing the sync, use the manual copy mode. This isn't quite as tedious as it sounds because the app understands the problem with duplicate file names, and it gives you the opportunity to deal with them.

Here's what you do. Set up a folder on the drive where you want to backup your phone's pictures. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone and copy them to this folder. Let's say you have 500 pictures. The copy will take a while, but you will eventually have all 500 pictures in that folder on the drive. Then a few days later, you want to backup your newer pictures, but you aren't sure exactly which ones are new. Do the same thing you did originally. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone, and tell the app to copy them to that same folder. After thinking about it for a while, it will tell you that you have selected 541 pictures to copy, but 500 of them have duplicate file names. It will ask you what you want to do about that. Select the "skip" option, and any file with a duplicate file name won't get copied. In this example, it will only copy the 41 pictures that weren't there before.

This works, but it's still not great. It takes a while to analyze the files before starting the copy. Let's say you had 1000 pictures originally, and you only took 2 new ones. The backup should be fast, right? Well, no. It takes the app a surprisingly long time to analyze the 1002 pictures and figure out that 1000 of them have duplicate file names. Eventually, it will tell you about the 1000 duplicates and you can select "skip". Then it will copy only the 2 new pictures. But even though there were only two new pictures, the process takes a frustratingly long time.

If you know exactly which pictures are new, and there aren't very many, you can always just pick those by hand instead of doing the select-all. In that case, the process is very fast since the app is only dealing with the few pictures you selected and not analyzing a 1000 of them.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57)

Waterproof Bone Conduction Headphones, IPX8 Waterproof 32GB Swimming MP3 Player Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.3 Open-ear Headphones with Mic for Swimming Skiing Cycling Driving Gym Workout(Black) PROS

1. These headphones are really different in appearance from regular earbud-type headphones, but they are oddly attractive in their design.

2. They are great for swimming in a pool or in any outdoor body of water, because they are extensively waterproof. They can be submerged to a depth of 20 meters (65 feet). This means they can be used for snorkeling and scuba diving.

3. They do not fit in the ear. Instead, sound is conducted through the cheekbone. I don’t understand the science behind this, but it does work.

6. This type of headphones are outstanding for safety purposes. People who walk, jog or run on public sidewalks or, especially, on deserted park paths/trails, are taking a big risk if they have their ears plugged with regular Bluetooth earbuds such that are not aware of sounds around them that could signal danger (e.g., a bike speeding down the park trail, careless skaters or skateboarders sharing the sidewalk and, worst of all, muggers).

6. A built-in microphone allows you to use the Bluetooth function to place and received calls on your cell phone.

7. These headphones are lightweight, durable, and flexible.

CONS

1. Other than for water sports and for safety purposes, these headphones are not as good as regular earbuds, because their sound quality is comparatively quite inferior.

2. Compared to regular Bluetooth earbuds, their price is very high.

text_fidelity_a:
Pioneer SP-BS22-LR Andrew Jones Home Audio Bookshelf Loudspeakers (Set of 2) If you're like me, you've done some research (extensively in my case) on comparing these two speakers, and have probably come out with a vague case for each of them. Some prefer the Miccas, some prefer the Pioneers. I decided to order both and find out what the deal is for myself. And although I haven't ordered many speakers, I've been a headphone enthusiast for many years.

FYI, I'm using these with a sub (Dayton 1200), so I can't comment on their performance by themselves.

The Miccas sound pretty good, with clear highs - solid performers for movies. But they never made me very impressed by their sound. They seem serviceable, good for the price but not particularly great. They are by no means a bad speaker, but they are a bit thin sounding, kind of one-note.

With the Miccas, if felt like I was listening to music, but with the Pioneers, I felt like I was feeling it. They have a lush tone that is very musical, and I noticed I was bobbing my head to some songs I wasn't before. Better dynamics, soundstage - they really allow you to get lost in the music. Even though the driver size is the same, everything sounds bigger, with more depth.

And even though they have less treble energy than the MB42X, they seem to retrieve a bit more detail. Certainly not "veiled", just darker in tone. I'd prefer there to be slightly less treble than too much - just make sure to remove the grill, as it can make them slightly too dark.

For $20 extra bucks currently I think it's a no-brainer to get the Pioneers, unless you can't particularly stand speakers on the warmer side. I have the center channel coming in today - I've heard mixed reports on it, but if it's anything like the bookshelves I'm sure I'll be satisfied.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer SP-BS22-LR Andrew Jones Home Audio Bookshelf Loudspeakers (Set of 2)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive) Sony WH-XB900N Wireless Noise Canceling Extra Bass Headphones have great sound quality. Plus, for an over the ear headphone they are surprisingly lightweight. I also like how they bend to fold up and are really pliable. However, that's really where the greatness stops. Pairing these with any device I own is difficult or doesn't happen at all. These will not pair with my laptop. My laptop sees it's there. It claims it's playing from the headphones, but alas it does not most of the time. In addition, these will not play from iTunes. So, if you have an Apple device forget it. These will not pair with my iPhone 5. For two reasons, first, these are terrible with Apple devices/software and second, you must have the App to pair the headphones, which if you have an older phone won't happen because the App is only compatible with certain iOS systems. As much as I am angry with Apple for stopping all updates for older Apple devices (which work just fine otherwise), it's equally frustrating with App developers who do not design their Apps to be compatible with the older systems. So, most of my experience with these headphones is through the AUX jack.

Therefore, the sound quality is really good. I listen to a lot of hiphop and the bass is spot on. However, I do listen other types of music (pretty much everything) and I would have to say listening to Beethoven's 6th and Old Blind Dogs was a nice experience as well! The noise cancelling is a joke. I can hear everything around me still. In fact, I'm currently wearing these as I type this review and can hear the click clack of the keys, my son bump around upstairs, and my father just call my name. So, if you wear these on public transportation or at work, you're gonna hear everything as usual. But they are good headphones and comfortable on my ears.

The instructions are ridiculous. Can we stop with the picture instructions? They make no sense. I need words and should not have to depend on internet video reviews to get clarity on how to use anything. There is a way to play, pause, volume down/up by tapping or swiping, but I have no idea how to do it. Sometimes it works, sometimes not. They have a long battery life. I charged these weeks ago and they still have a charge as I use them now.

So, these have a great sound quality, the noise cancellation doesn't do anything, and you need to pair these with non-Apple devices.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202) I expect that no one is going to use a stylus 100% of the time with their touch screen. There are, however, some times when a stylus is more convenient than using your finger. Drawing objects freehand is a common example. Another example is when you need to precisely move objects around the screen (eg in a CAD program) and this is difficult with your finger because your finger blocks your view of the target area.

There are many many touch screen stylus for sale on Amazon. Some cost less than 50 cents each. All the latest stylus have similar round soft touch rubber tips. All seem to work about the same. This iHome stylus doesn't seem to work any better than the others that I have tried.

The iHome stylus is better looking than most of the competition because of the long slim shape with silver-tone accents. Some of the cheap ones look very plasticy (though they do work just as well). Some other stylus are fatter, which makes them easier to grip if you have large hands.

The built-in ball-point pen is a feature that most other stylus do not have. The pen works well, though I do not know how easy ink refills will be to find. There is no literature in the package about what refills it can use.

Is this product worth $15? I have to say no, but I'm a cheapskate. You can decide on value for yourself, but look at the competition first.
text_fidelity_b: iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202)

Soundcore Anker Life Q20 Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Over Ear Bluetooth Headphones, 40H Playtime, Hi-Res Audio, Deep Bass, Memory Foam Ear Cups, for Travel, Home Office Wow! I was impressed by these headphones. Not only do they have clear sound, but they are comfortable for longer listening times. They make listening to something easy even when the train in the valley is going by, or the trash trucks are at work.
I don't usually use the noise cancellation since the headphones cancel a lot of noise anyway, but turning on the noise cancellation was astonishing! It cut out so much noise that I didn't know when the AC kicked on and wondered why I suddenly felt my chair vibrate just a little. I can completely understand why there are cautions about using the noise cancellation at times because you really can't hear much!
I charged my headphones one week, and it is still fully charged a week later. Of course I don't listen all the time or for hours on end, but it's great that I don't have to charge them all the time.
One thing I really like about these, besides the comfort and noise blocking, is the fact that they are wireless. I like to be able to get up and move away from my computer and still keep listening.
I'm very glad I got these!

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens Bulk packaging (White box, New) An upgrade of Nikon's original digital-only tele kit zoom, this new 55-200mm f/4-5.6 ($250, street) adds Vibration Reduction and a number of optical improvements for only $70 more. A 3.6X 82-300mm equivalent zoom, it's not expected to be bundled in Nikon DSLR kits any time soon.

Hands on:

The barrel, when contracted, is nearly an inch longer than the earlier 55-200mm non-VR DX lens, but is still extremely light as a result of all-plastic construction, including the lensmount. The large zoom ring's slightly uneven and underdamped turning action is what you'd expect from a lens at this price. The narrow manual-focusing ring is even-turning but also underdamped, with a very short turning radius for fast, if coarse, manual focusing. AF action on our test camera, the D40x, was adequately fast and quiet, thanks to Nikon's Silent Wave Motor in the lens.

In the lab:

SQF tests found Excellent sharpness and contrast at all focal lengths -- an improvement over the earlier, non-VR version of this lens. DxO Analyzer 2.0 tests found Imperceptible barrel distortion at 55mm (0.08%), and Slight pincushion distortion at 105mm and 200mm (0.24% and 0.19%, respectively). All three are also improvements over the earlier lens. Light falloff was gone from the corners by f/5 at 55mm, f/7.1 at 105mm, and f/8 at 200mm.

At the uniform close-focusing distance of approximately 43.5 inches, tests of close-up ability found maximum magnification ratios ranging from 1:14.25 at 55mm to 1:3.8 at 200mm, about an average magnifying power, and not up to the 1:3.4 turned in by the non-VR 55-200mm. DxO Analyzer Blur tests of the lens' first-generation VR system (at 200mm) showed an improvement for three users of about 3 stops of extra handheld sharpness at slower shutter speeds; 4 stops are possible with Nikon's VR II system.

Conclusions:

Even though it's the earlier version of VR, to get any VR at this price is a steal.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens Bulk packaging (White box, New)

ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs What I like about this monitor:
1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.
2. Very clear resolution despite having an old video card.
3. It has an HDMI connection but I am using the regular VGA input and it still very clear.
4. A VGA and sound cord are included.
5. Very sleek, streamline black design which goes nicely with my other computer accessories.

What could be better:
1. The included instructions tell you nothing about how to make video and audio adjustments. I can't use a bright setting and it took a good while to figure out how to use the buttons underneath the screen. They are not intuitive at all.
2. Poor Audio - if you want good audio from this monitor that will not be possible. It is a thin monitor and the audio is very thin and tinny. I was hoping I could disconnect my external sound system to make more room on my desk but found out that I must keep it if I want to hear any decent sound from my computer.
3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.

text_fidelity_a: Echo Show 8 (2nd Gen, 2021 release) - Glacier White - with 30-day FREE trial of Alexa Together (monthly auto-renewal) This is not a good unit. I would recommend purchasing the echo show 5. There is absolutely no way to adjust the clock face on this unit. There is no way to adjust the night clock face on this unit either. I bought this unit so that I would have a larger smart clock in my living room. What a mistake that was. I have 2 echo show 5 units that are excellent. The clocks are actually smaller on the larger screened 8 than on the 5. I simply could not believe it. So I called customer service immediately and it's true. There is no way to adjust the clock faces on the 8. So unless you're just interested in the bigger picture, I recommend skipping this unit because I would not want you to be sitting here like I am tonight writing this and being so disappointed at an obvious flaw that should've been fixed long ago with a simple firmware upgrade. I am returning this unit first thing in the morning.
